non_2xx_http_status.reader_path: EmuReady.request() line 153: if (!response.isSuccessful) throw IOException("EmuReady request failed with HTTP <code>")
non_2xx_http_status.ui_effect: CommunityReportsButton catches Exception -> failed=true -> string vapor_community_unavailable: 'Could not reach EmuReady. You can still play your game…'
non_2xx_http_status.nuance: These are HTTP-level failures by design even when the body is a structured trpc error; the UI wording is the network-failure wording, and no unexpected-response wording appears.

200_with_envelope_result_data_json.ui_effect: normal data rendering (or an empty page / empty reports state)
live_examples: unknown-but-valid gameId -> empty listings page (no exception)

200_with_broken_or_missing_envelope.reader_path: envelope() throws UnexpectedResponseException; also >2 MiB body -> UnexpectedResponseException
200_with_broken_or_missing_envelope.ui_effect: unexpected=true -> string vapor_community_unexpected: 'EmuReady returned a response this app does not understand…'
200_with_broken_or_missing_envelope.grounding: Not producible with the public procedures: every 200 response was valid result.data.json. Branch grounded in code lines 132-134 and committed tests (CommunityReportsUiTest.anUnexpectedResponseHasItsOwnWordingSeparateFromAConnectionError).

conclusions: The mobile path accepts OkHttp 5.3.2's default UA exactly as the app sends it (200, payload byte-identical to the browser-UA control).
No header/UA workaround is needed by the app; the earlier 403 in docs/QUALIFICATION.md was the desktop path /api/trpc (origin/session gate), not the mobile path (see the earlier re-check receipt).

Every malformed/oversized input the server rejects is an HTTP non-2xx status, so the reader reports it as the connection-error state; only a 200 body that breaks the envelope reaches the unexpected-response state, and that state was not observable live.

confirmed.statement: The signed-out app reached live EmuReady Windows reports for Half-Life 2 and loaded one report's live settings; values on screen match the live API payloads exactly. No injected fixtures or simulated data were used.

Live malformed/missing/unknown/oversized inputs return HTTP 400/404/431 JSON errors; the reader classifies all of these as IOException (connection-failure wording), not UnexpectedResponseException. A valid 200 envelope with an unknown gameId is an empty page, not an error.
The app's effective default UA (OkHttp 5.3.2) is accepted by the mobile EmuReady path; browser and OkHttp UA responses are byte-identical.

Team Fortress 2 in the real catalog shows Community reports, and the modal reports 'No matching Windows entry found. This does not mean the game is incompatible.' after live batch not_found + empty title search.
Browse on EmuReady and Read original report resolve to Chrome with the reader-generated URLs (listings?search=Half-Life%202 and listings/d925bc70-…), not to invented URLs.
For Windows catalog apps the Community reports action is present (Half-Life 2 and Team Fortress 2), consistent with the windows != false rule.
The settings view is text-only; no apply/import control exists and nothing was applied. No game was launched.

limitations: Single observation window (2026-10-21, ~18:57-19:23 UTC) and a single emulated environment; upstream Steam/EmuReady data drifts.
Emulator only: no physical phone, no TalkBack/accessibility pass, no physical gamepad.
The emulator ran with -memory 2048 (host pressure) rather than the briefed 3072, and in landscape orientation; performance of the UI under memory pressure was slow at times.
The custom clone AVD (Vapor_API_36_live) is not the exact Vapor_API_36 AVD instance, though it uses the same system image, pixel_7 profile, API 36 and a 2 GB guest.
First-run setup (file access + ~127 MB game support) was performed on this fresh emulator; that is unrelated to the EmuReady feature but was required before Store access.
Only one live report card and one settings payload were inspected in the UI; the underlying payload has 8 Windows reports for Half-Life 2, all validated by the earlier API re-check.
Chrome showed its first-run screen for both browser handoffs, so the EmuReady web pages themselves were not rendered in this pass (the intent URLs were confirmed from the WindowManager capturedLink).
The Windows-less gating branch and the 200-broken-envelope branch were not observable live (see not_validated_live).
No Steam sign-in, purchase, license grant, download, game launch or settings application was attempted.
follow_up_needs: If the gating negative branch must be proven live, find a real Steam catalog app whose store item has platforms.windows=false (e.g. via an official Steam data source) and repeat the catalog-details step on it.
For a physical-device confirmation, repeat steps 7-10 on hardware with TalkBack to cover accessibility and real network conditions.
Re-run the journey on a later date to detect upstream drift in reports/settings values.
Consider capturing the EmuReady web pages after Chrome's first-run setup is completed, so the browser handoff is visually confirmed (this pass only proved the Intent URL).
